affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
implementationRisks.title: Common dashboard layout currently performs legacy reads and effects before any SUPER_USER shell branch

sourceEvidence.explanation: Current implementation derives legacy institute scope before any explicit SUPER_USER branch.
Activity and Knowledge Exchange eligibility services are invoked before shell selection.
Legacy enrollment/course titles and codes are queried before rendering the shell.
Login-reward processing and gamification reads precede the existing DashboardLayout render.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, a SUPER_USER request can enter legacy eligibility, course, gamification, and shell preparation rather than receiving the isolated AcademicOperationsShell. This is an unimplemented baseline exposure, not a defect in the revised design.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement the specified canonical-session and supported-institute checks, then branch on explicit role before every legacy read or effect. Pass SUPER_USER only the approved oversight DTO and basic own identity to a dedicated shell.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
implementationRisks.title: Current course layout reads private course data before complete role, institute, and relationship authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The layout reads the course, instructor name, and pending-enrollment count using courseId alone before authorization.
The current check does not explicitly reject SUPER_USER or unknown roles and does not bind the course query to the route institute.
Pending submission counts are queried after only the incomplete instructor/Admin classification.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implementation, a SUPER_USER assigned as instructor, an unrecognized role with enrollment, or a cross-institute course identifier may reach legacy course data and derived counts.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Apply the revised design literally: recognize only the canonical normal-role set, deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before private reads, resolve Course with both courseId and actual institute, and establish instructor assignment, approved enrollment, or Admin authority before counts, headers, tabs, or children.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
implementationRisks.title: Sandbox remains an unguarded client page with hard-coded submission identities

sourceEvidence.explanation: The existing page is a client component and therefore cannot perform the required server-leaf authentication itself.
The page is described as dev-only and defines hard-coded student and assignment identifiers.
Those hard-coded identifiers are passed to SubmitBar, exposing a mutation-capable flow to caller-controlled client execution.

implementationRisks.impact: Until the planned extraction is implemented, direct navigation can load the client activity and attempt submissions using identities that are not bound to the authenticated actor or persisted authorized template/course relationship.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Create the specified server wrapper at the existing page path, reject SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before rendering, extract current UI into the allowlisted legacy-client component, and ensure every submission API independently binds the real actor, institute, template, course, enrollment, and owned attempt.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
implementationRisks.title: Existing shared shell components fall unknown and SUPER_USER roles into legacy Admin or Student navigation and mount forbidden widgets

sourceEvidence.explanation: The existing dashboard always mounts Sidebar, Topbar, and MobileBottomNav for every supplied role.
Any role other than instructor aliases or ADMIN falls back to Student links, so SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN currently receive student navigation.
Any role other than Student or the two recognized instructor aliases receives Admin tabs.
Only Student and PROFESSOR/TEACHER are distinguished.
The fallback selects Admin items, exposing account, permission, and audit-log navigation to SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN.
The legacy topbar mounts search, settings, and NotificationBell controls.
The legacy user menu exposes profile, settings, privacy, help, and logout rather than the exact Super User support surface.

implementationRisks.impact: Until the separate oversight shell is implemented, role fallbacks can present legacy Student/Admin affordances, notifications, profile/settings links, search, and other features explicitly excluded from the Super User contract. UI links are not authority, but they expand exposure and bypass the intended least-privilege shell.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Never pass SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN into the legacy DashboardLayout component tree. Implement a dedicated AcademicOperationsShell containing only approved scope selection, oversight navigation, own basic identity, and logout; also make legacy role selection fail closed for defense in depth and include the INSTRUCTOR alias where normal-role behavior requires it.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
implementationRisks.title: Current institute landing page has no SUPER_USER redirect and displays an unknown-role response

sourceEvidence.explanation: Only STUDENT, PROFESSOR/TEACHER, and ADMIN are redirected; all other roles receive the Unknown role JSX response.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, an authenticated SUPER_USER visiting an institute root does not reach that institute's academic-operations destination, and the INSTRUCTOR alias also lacks its intended normal-role redirect.
implementationRisks.recommendation: After canonical authentication and supported-institute validation, redirect SUPER_USER to the same requested institute's academic-operations route, retain the stated ICS initial-login behavior at the login destination, map the canonical INSTRUCTOR alias to the instructor landing, and fail UNKNOWN closed without private props.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
implementationRisks.title: Middleware currently treats cookie presence as sufficient routing assistance and omits Bearer-only page requests

sourceEvidence.explanation: The middleware checks only whether lumina_session is present; it neither validates the session nor recognizes a Bearer credential for page routing.
All cookie-bearing requests continue regardless of token validity, confirming that server leaves must remain the final authority.

implementationRisks.impact: Stale or forged cookie values reach server routes, while a Bearer-only page request may be redirected. The revised design correctly removes middleware from final authority, but this baseline remains until server leaves consistently authenticate and the desired routing compatibility is implemented.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Keep middleware non-authoritative as designed. Ensure every assigned server layout/page uses the canonical cookie-first, Bearer-fallback resolver and does not depend on middleware admission; preserve or explicitly implement Bearer-compatible routing assistance if page access is part of the transitional contract.

implementationRisks.title: Production disclosure remains intentionally blocked by unassigned operational trust and dataset controls

sourceEvidence.symbol: META-01 exact disclosure and operational contract / Operational decisions
sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied document explicitly leaves the trusted academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset identity/fingerprint and attestation procedure, approval lifetime, and revocation publication owner/runbook as required human or operator assignments.

implementationRisks.impact: No production metadata approval can be trusted or admitted until these identities and procedures are assigned. Under the specified deny-by-default behavior, the exact blocking effect is that oversight reads must return the safe METADATA_REVIEW_REQUIRED failure and serialize no DTO; deployment cannot claim usable production disclosure.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Before production disclosure, governance must name the institution-designated approver and independent manifest maintainer/reviewer, establish the real production dataset fingerprint and attestation procedure, choose approval lifetimes, and own a coordinated revocation publication runbook. Do not invent these values; retain deny-by-default until supplied.

coverage.assessment: The revised design appropriately retains middleware only for routing and security headers and explicitly excludes it from final authorization. Current cookie-presence behavior is recorded as an unresolved implementation risk.

The revised role-before-read branch, supported-institute validation, canonical session selection, and isolated AcademicOperationsShell are architecturally coherent. Existing pre-branch reads and effects remain unremediated.

The design clearly distinguishes root landing redirection from child authorization and preserves the requested institute for explicit SUPER_USER roots. Existing SUPER_USER and INSTRUCTOR fallback behavior remains unimplemented.

The revised boundary requires recognized normal role, route-institute-bound course resolution, and persisted assignment/enrollment before any private course read, count, header, tab, or child. This adequately addresses the current baseline exposure.

The explicit server-wrapper and allowlisted legacy-client extraction design provides an appropriate server leaf boundary while preserving client UI behavior. Independent API/action authorization remains mandatory.

The revised design does not reuse this legacy shell for SUPER_USER and prohibits its legacy widgets and providers. Current unconditional legacy component mounting is an unresolved implementation risk.

The design excludes this legacy topbar from the SUPER_USER shell and separately specifies scope routing and logout. Current notification, search, profile, settings, privacy, help, and path-preserving campus switching behavior is not remediated.
The revised design prohibits mounting the legacy sidebar for SUPER_USER. The existing default-to-Student role behavior remains an unresolved fail-open presentation risk.
The revised design prohibits this component in the SUPER_USER shell. The existing fallback to Admin tabs for unknown and SUPER_USER roles remains unremediated.

The revised design expressly excludes Mobile More, Admin fallback, profile/settings, and unrelated navigation while retaining logout in the dedicated shell. Current fallback behavior remains an unresolved implementation risk.

limitations: This was a document-only pre-implementation design review. No product implementation, runtime behavior, tests, database transaction, import graph, manifest, or deployment state was inspected or claimed.

The supplied revised architecture document was not line-numbered; evidence for its operational-assignment section is therefore identified by exact document path and section symbol with the only available document line position.

The referenced exact revised file allowlist and boundary-matrix files were described but not supplied as separate document bodies. Review was limited to the ten explicitly assigned paths, their supplied sanitized source, the supplied page rows relevant to those paths, and necessary shared policy.
No HTTP methods or action exports were assigned in this subset, so none are claimed as reviewed.
